strengths: The paper addresses a relevant and challenging problem: generating follower motion conditioned on both leader motion and music, with attention to interaction detail and extended sequence generation.
The reported improvements over Duolando are substantial on several metrics: FIDk improves from 54.39 to 41.61, FIDg from 26.64 to 10.95, FIDcd from 17.46 to 8.24, and BED from 0.3042 to 0.3676.

The evaluation includes motion, interaction, and musical alignment metrics, component ablations, and a small user study reporting 68.7% preference over Duolando. The masking and residual-depth ablations provide useful preliminary evidence for the design.
weaknesses: The central long-term coherence claim is insufficiently supported. Section 3.4 explicitly isolates blocks but does not explain how sampled boundary states are coordinated across blocks. Overlapping training windows alone do not ensure continuity during generation. Aggregate FID results do not establish elimination of error accumulation; boundary discontinuity measurements and quality-versus-duration experiments are needed. The claimed efficiency also lacks runtime or memory measurements.

Important mathematical details are problematic as written. Equation (1) computes the third quantized component from the first and second quantized outputs rather than the remaining encoder residual, conflicting with the stated cumulative residual reconstruction. Equation (5) introduces learnable loss weights without specifying constraints or regularization that prevent weight collapse or an unbounded objective. These may be exposition errors, but they affect verification of the core algorithm.

The novelty and semantic interpretation of the hierarchy are not convincingly established. GRFSQ combines acknowledged scalar quantization and grouped residual quantization ideas, while LDCFG applies separate guidance weights to residual components. Neither residual refinement nor the aggregate metric changes in Table 4 demonstrate disentanglement between body-level rhythm and joint-level detail. Controlled interventions showing what each scale changes are missing.

Comparative evaluation is limited. Duolando is the only directly matched dance-accompaniment baseline. The adaptation of text-conditioned InterGen to leader-motion and music conditioning is insufficiently described, and its reported fixed-window failure makes its poor performance difficult to interpret. The VQ replacement does not isolate quantizer choice, grouping, residual structure, or representation capacity; comparisons with matched residual VQ and simpler latent-diffusion configurations would better establish the contribution.

Several reporting inconsistencies undermine confidence in the ablations. Section 4.3 apparently uses the VQ BAS value of 0.2122 as BED when claiming a 42% reduction. Table 2's caption reports Divg=34.27 without progressive masking, whereas its row reports 6.79. The R=2 and w/o BLC configurations also have identical values across all five reported metrics despite representing different ablations. These results require verification and correction.

The evidence is confined to the 1.95-hour DD100 dataset, without repeated-run uncertainty or confidence intervals. The user study has only 15 participants evaluating 15 video pairs, with unclear allocation across comparisons. Broader synchronization and physical-realism claims exceed the measurements: BAS is lower than Duolando's (0.1944 versus 0.2089), and foot sliding, contact accuracy, and interpenetration are not quantified.

Reproducibility is insufficient despite reporting hardware, optimizers, and training durations. Essential settings are missing, including quantization levels, group counts and latent dimensions, the complete GRFSQ training objective, masking parameters, diffusion sampling configuration, and conditioning-dropout procedure. Together with the unresolved technical and evaluation issues, this leaves the submission below the acceptance threshold.
